plan.title: pre-push branch gate (preflight_branch.py) false-positives on branch deletions / feature-branch pushes when HEAD is the default branch

narratives.Description: pre-push branch gate (preflight_branch.py) false-positives on branch deletions / feature-branch pushes when HEAD is the default branch
narratives.Overview:
## Summary
The pre-push branch-protection gate (#747) blocks pushes based on the **local current branch** rather than what is actually being pushed. When your local `HEAD` is the default branch (`main`/`master`), *any* `git push` is refused — including `git push origin --delete <feature-branch>`, which creates no commit on the default branch at all. This is a false positive that misclassifies a harmless operation as a protected-branch violation.

## Environment
- Framework version: `v0.52.0` (sha `6b8679d`), vendored into a consumer repo via `deft-install`.
- Files involved:
  - `.githooks/pre-push` (line ~114)
  - `scripts/preflight_branch.py` (canonical: `.deft/core/scripts/preflight_branch.py`)

## Reproduction
From a consumer repo, while checked out on `main`:

```
$ git push origin --delete some/already-merged-feature-branch
❌ deft branch-protection: refusing to commit/push directly to the default branch 'main' (#747).
  ...
error: failed to push some refs
```

The delete removes a non-default feature branch and adds nothing to `main`, yet it is blocked.

## Root cause
`.githooks/pre-push` invokes the two gates like so:

```sh
deft_py "$SCRIPTS_DIR/preflight_branch.py" --project-root "$REPO_ROOT" || exit $?   # gate #1
deft_py "$SCRIPTS_DIR/preflight_gh.py" --pre-push-stdin                             # gate #2
```

- **Gate #1 (`preflight_branch.py`)** is passed only `--project-root`. It decides purely from `git symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD` (`_current_branch`) and blocks whenever that is a default branch. It never reads the per-ref stdin, so it cannot distinguish "commit to main" from "delete a feature branch" or "push a feature branch while HEAD happens to be main."
- **Gate #2 (`preflight_gh.py --pre-push-stdin`)** *does* read the per-ref stdin lines and correctly only blocks destructive default-branch operations (e.g. force-push to `main`). But the hook exits at gate #1 (`|| exit $?`) before ever reaching it.

## Empirical confirmation
Same repo, the only variable is the current branch:

| Test | Branch / input | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A) `preflight_branch.py` | on `main` | ❌ "refusing to … push directly to the default branch 'main'" |
| B) `preflight_branch.py` | on a feature branch | ✅ "feature branch … proceeding" |
| C) `preflight_gh.py --pre-push-stdin` | fed the real delete refspec `(delete) 0…0 refs/heads/<feature> <sha>` | ✅ "no pushes to default branches detected — proceeding" (exit 0) |

Gate #2 — the one that actually inspects the push — approves the delete. The block came solely from gate #1 keying off the current branch.

## Impact
- Users on `main` cannot delete already-merged branches or push feature branches without hitting a misleading "refusing to commit to default branch" error.
- The documented recovery ("create a feature branch", `task policy:allow-direct-commits`, or `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT=1`) is confusing because the user was never trying to commit to the default branch.
- Encourages reaching for the env-var bypass for benign operations, eroding the gate's signal.

## Suggested fix
In the **pre-push** context, gate the actual refspecs instead of (or in addition to) the current branch:

- Option A: In `.githooks/pre-push`, rely on gate #2 (`preflight_gh.py --pre-push-stdin`) for push-time default-branch protection and do not run the current-branch-only gate #1 at pre-push time. (Gate #1 remains correct at pre-commit time, where "current branch" is exactly what matters.)
- Option B: Teach `preflight_branch.py` a pre-push mode that reads the per-ref stdin and only blocks refs that would *add commits to* a default branch (i.e. `<remote_ref>` is a default branch AND `<local_oid>` is non-zero / not a delete), leaving feature-branch pushes and deletions alone.

Either way, deletions (zero local OID) and pushes whose remote ref is not a default branch should pass regardless of which branch `HEAD` is on.

## Workarounds (for now)
- Run the delete from a non-default branch, or
- Delete via the GitHub API/UI (bypasses local hooks), or
- `DEFT_ALLOW_DEFAULT_BRANCH_COMMIT=1 git push origin --delete <branch>`.
